limitations: Six legacy task modules under packages/main/src/tasks are kept unregistered with printed reasons (legacy @task pipeline pinned by the silent-catch baseline; a hand-run generator; a fixture loader) and belong to a dead-code cleanup. The RED guard is a commit-subject convention: it cannot tie a RED subject to a real failing run, so a fabricated RED still passes; the story-qualified allowance only removes cross-story collisions. Load-flaky heartbeat smokes seen in the C story's gates are recorded in dev-memory for a later owner, not changed here.
pitfalls: Four implementers worked one worktree in parallel; disjoint files and per-path git add kept it clean, but the tier-planner digest pin had to be re-pinned after CHK-001 registered a new command. The pinned CHK-002 edge selector was vacuous until the print was moved behind the edge assertion (pins are immutable, so the line text could not change). The prior-RED allowance went through two designs: merge-base history first (F-006), then story-qualified ids only after the behavior lane showed an unrelated story's RED(CHK-001) satisfying a branch GREEN and the agy host showed the unbounded git log overflowing maxBuffer into a silently empty set (F-007, F-008). Three REVIEW rounds, eight findings.
